samples.summary: A row scrolled past now leaves a glyph-subset @font-face connected for that family, so document text using the family renders half-real / half-fallback (previously scrolling loaded the whole family)
samples.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` injects `css2?family=X:wght@N&text=<label glyphs>`. Google's `&text=` response has NO `unicode-range`, so the face applies to every codepoint of family X. Nothing else in the app loads a full link for a family merely present in the document: `useGoogleFontsLink()` (docs-view.tsx:213, slides-view.tsx:230) only requests `eager` families, and `ensureFontLink` is called only on apply/hover (apply-font-family.ts:28, theme-builder-panel.tsx:100, toolbar `onPrefetch`). So for a reloaded doc that uses a non-eager family, the pre-change behaviour was "scroll the picker → full family arrives → canvas repairs"; now scrolling injects only the label's glyphs, and the canvas/DOM paints those glyphs in the real face and every other character per-glyph fallback — mixed faces and inconsistent measurement, and the subset link is never removed unless a full link later loads (font-catalog.ts:197).

samples.summary: Call site that the new "await ensureFontLink before check()/load()" contract protects, but does not await: FontRegistry.ensureFont can mark a family 'loaded' off the preview subset
samples.evidence: font-catalog.ts:155 states the returned promise MUST be awaited before `document.fonts.load()`/`check()`, and pdf-actions.ts:47 does. This call site does not: `ensureFontLink(family); store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family);` runs the registry synchronously after injecting the link. `FontRegistry.ensureFont` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302) does `if (document.fonts.check('12px "X"')) { status='loaded'; return; }` — with the picker's subset face connected and already painted (its glyphs include the space in labels like "Open Sans"), `check()` answers true, the family is permanently recorded as loaded, `document.fonts.load()` for the real face is never issued and no re-layout listener fires. (Impact is currently masked because `editor.getStore().fonts` is an unwired stub, per docs/tasks/.../docs-font-controls-lessons.md — so today the second line no-ops.)

samples.summary: The 5s race abandons the stylesheet wait but not the subset face, so a slow network still exports a deck rasterised from preview glyphs
samples.evidence: `Promise.race([...ensureFontLink…, setTimeout(5000)])` — the subset link is only removed inside `ensureFontLink`'s settle handler (font-catalog.ts:197). If the timeout wins, the subset face for a previewed family is still connected and `document.fonts.load(`16px "X"`)` on line 54 resolves against it, which is exactly the "deck exports with only the glyphs a dropdown row painted" failure the header comment says this change prevents. A cheap fix is to drop preview links for the exported families before the `fonts.load` loop rather than only on full-link load.

samples.summary: Preview idempotency is keyed on family only, ignoring `text`, so a later row needing MORE glyphs is silently served the earlier, insufficient subset
samples.evidence: `if (findPreviewFontLink(family)) return;` — the picker row's subset is the label alone, the dialog row's is label + group name (more-fonts-dialog.tsx:151 passes `row.textContent`, covering the inherited group span). Scroll the dropdown past "Lobster" first and the later dialog row's "Display" text has no glyphs in the subset, so it paints in a fallback face while the label paints in Lobster. No union/re-request path exists.

samples.summary: On a FAILED full stylesheet the settle handler still removes the preview link, destroying the only working face for that row
samples.evidence: Both `load` and `error` resolve the promise, and the `.then()` unconditionally calls `removePreviewFontLink(family)`. When the full request errors (e.g. a bad `wght@` for a single-cut family, or offline), the subset was the only real face the row had; deleting it regresses a previously-correct preview to fallback. The removal should be conditional on the `load` path.

samples.summary: `ensureFontLink` resolves immediately for an existing link with no recorded promise, so a caller can proceed before the stylesheet has parsed (and the subset is never dropped)
samples.evidence: `if (existing) return fullLinkSettled.get(existing) ?? Promise.resolve();` — the fallback resolves synchronously even though the link's request may still be in flight. Any caller relying on the documented contract (pdf-actions.ts:47) then queries the Font Loading API in exactly the window the doc comment warns about, and because the settle handler never runs for that link, the family's preview subset stays connected for the session. Reachable whenever module state and the DOM disagree (HMR, a second bundle instance of the module).

samples.summary: `hasFullFamilyLink` only scans `document.head`, so a full-family stylesheet injected anywhere else is invisible and a shrinking subset can still be added
samples.evidence: `document.head.querySelectorAll('link[rel="stylesheet"]')` — a `<link>` in `<body>` (legal, and how some component libraries / Vite dev-injected styles land) or a `@import`ed css2 sheet is not seen, so the guard the doc comment describes as "ANY full css2 link in the head" is exactly that: head-only. The stated consequence of missing one is removing glyphs and the bold cut from a family that already had them.

samples.summary: The race's timer is never cleared
samples.evidence: `new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, FONT_CSS_TIMEOUT_MS))` — when the font promises win, a 5s timer stays pending with no `clearTimeout`. Harmless in a browser tab, but it keeps a macrotask alive past the export and will hold a test/jsdom environment open for 5s if this function is ever unit-tested.

samples.summary: `previewWeight` can return two weights, contradicting its "single weight" contract
samples.evidence: `const first = (weights ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS).split(';')[0].trim(); return first || DEFAULT_WEIGHTS;` — for `weights` of `''` or `';400'` the fallback returns `'400;700'`, so the preview requests two cuts (and, for a single-cut family whose spec was malformed, a 400 that css2 rejects with an error page).

samples.summary: `// @ts-check` in the new shared helper is not actually checked, and `walk`'s parameter is untyped
samples.evidence: packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json `include` is `["src", "test", "vite.shell.config.ts"]`, so `scripts/**` is never in the program — the pragma at line 1 is decorative (the same thing that tsconfig's own comment calls "worse than no pragma"). Correspondingly `const walk = (dir) => {` has no `@param`, unlike the copies kept in verify-scenes.mjs/verify-tokens.mjs. Also the `ARTEFACTS` JSDoc says "Everything the two artefacts are built from", which describes the sources, not the artefact list it annotates.

finding.summary: A row scrolled past now leaves a glyph-subset @font-face connected for that family, so document text using the family renders half-real / half-fallback (previously scrolling loaded the whole family)
finding.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` injects `css2?family=X:wght@N&text=<label glyphs>`. Google's `&text=` response has NO `unicode-range`, so the face applies to every codepoint of family X. Nothing else in the app loads a full link for a family merely present in the document: `useGoogleFontsLink()` (docs-view.tsx:213, slides-view.tsx:230) only requests `eager` families, and `ensureFontLink` is called only on apply/hover (apply-font-family.ts:28, theme-builder-panel.tsx:100, toolbar `onPrefetch`). So for a reloaded doc that uses a non-eager family, the pre-change behaviour was "scroll the picker → full family arrives → canvas repairs"; now scrolling injects only the label's glyphs, and the canvas/DOM paints those glyphs in the real face and every other character per-glyph fallback — mixed faces and inconsistent measurement, and the subset link is never removed unless a full link later loads (font-catalog.ts:197).

verdict.reason: The described code exists as claimed and no guard blocks the path. `ensurePreviewFontLink` (font-catalog.ts:305-331) injects a `&text=` subset link whose face, per the module's own comments (font-catalog.ts:218-225, 250-259), carries no `unicode-range` and therefore applies to every codepoint of the family. Its guards (SSR, system, eager, existing preview link, `hasFullFamilyLink` at font-catalog.ts:261-280) only skip when a FULL link already exists; a family used by the open document but never fully linked passes all of them. Both row observers invoke it on scroll-into-view (font-family-picker.tsx:138-165 incl. the Recent rows at :241-270; more-fonts-dialog.tsx:138-165). Nothing loads a full link for a family merely present in a reloaded document: `useGoogleFontsLink` -> `buildGoogleFontsHref` requests only `eager` families (font-catalog.ts:112-116; docs-view.tsx:213, slides-view.tsx:230), and every `ensureFontLink` call site is apply/hover/export (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:350, apply-font-family.ts:28, theme-builder-panel.tsx:100, text-edit-section.tsx:68, mobile-toolbar.tsx:554, pdf-actions.ts:48). `FontRegistry.ensureFont` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:293) only calls `document.fonts.load()` and injects no link. The subset link's sole removal path is `removePreviewFontLink`, called only after a full link settles (font-catalog.ts:191-198), so nothing cleans it up on picker close. Result: mixed real/fallback glyph rendering and inconsistent measurement for document text in that family — a real, user-visible behavioral bug in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Call site that the new "await ensureFontLink before check()/load()" contract protects, but does not await: FontRegistry.ensureFont can mark a family 'loaded' off the preview subset
finding.evidence: font-catalog.ts:155 states the returned promise MUST be awaited before `document.fonts.load()`/`check()`, and pdf-actions.ts:47 does. This call site does not: `ensureFontLink(family); store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family);` runs the registry synchronously after injecting the link. `FontRegistry.ensureFont` (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302) does `if (document.fonts.check('12px "X"')) { status='loaded'; return; }` — with the picker's subset face connected and already painted (its glyphs include the space in labels like "Open Sans"), `check()` answers true, the family is permanently recorded as loaded, `document.fonts.load()` for the real face is never issued and no re-layout listener fires. (Impact is currently masked because `editor.getStore().fonts` is an unwired stub, per docs/tasks/.../docs-font-controls-lessons.md — so today the second line no-ops.)

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:350-354 calls ensureFontLink(family) without await, then store.fonts?.ensureFont?.(family); font-catalog.ts:155 states the await contract; fonts.ts:302 does the check()/'loaded' shortcut). But the harmful operation is unreachable from this call site: the registry call is behind double optional chaining and no store in the repo exposes `fonts`. The DocStore interface (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:11+) declares no `fonts` member, MemDocStore and YorkieDocStore contain no `fonts` (grep over packages/docs/src/store and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts returns nothing), and editor.getStore() returns exactly that store (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:925, 2744). FontRegistry is never instantiated in product code at all — repo-wide grep finds it only at its definition (packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:278), its re-export (packages/docs/src/index.ts:188), and a unit test (packages/docs/test/view/fonts.test.ts:63). Therefore document.fonts.check() is never invoked inside the un-awaited window from this path, no family can be recorded as 'loaded' off the preview subset, and no load()/re-layout is skipped. The finding itself concedes the impact is masked; a latent contract gap that would only fire if a future change wires `fonts` onto DocStore is not a current crash/wrong-behavior/data-loss path under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: `verify-frame.mjs` still builds only the shell, so it hits exactly the `Cannot find module …/dist/plugin/index.js` / stale-plugin trap this PR fixes in its three sibling scripts
finding.evidence: This PR updated `verify-consumer.mjs` (same package), `verify-scenes.mjs` and `verify-tokens.mjs` to build BOTH artefacts, on the stated grounds that `exports["."]` now names `dist/plugin/index.js` and the fixture's `vite.config.ts` imports the package by name. `verify-frame.mjs` boots the SAME fixture — `const PROJECT = path.join(PKG, 'fixtures/consumer')` (line 46), and `fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts:17` does `import { designEditor, cssVariables } from '@wafflebase/design-editor'` — but `buildShellIfStale()` (lines 82-91) still runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts`, and `newestSourceMtime()` (line 106) still only stats `vite.shell.config.ts`, not `tsconfig.build.json`. On a clean checkout `boot()` therefore throws `dev server exited early: … Cannot find module`, reported as a broken fixture; on a dirty checkout every browser check runs against plugin bytes older than the change under test — the precise failure mode the diff's own comments call "worse than no gate".

verdict.reason: The claimed omission does not exist in the working tree. verify-frame.mjs:43 imports `buildDesignEditorIfStale` from the shared helper `./build-if-stale.mjs`, and verify-frame.mjs:122 calls it as the first statement of `main()`, before `boot()` starts vite on the fixture. That helper builds BOTH artefacts, not just the shell: build-if-stale.mjs:40 declares `ARTEFACTS = ['dist/shell/index.html', 'dist/plugin/index.js']`, :67-71 treats either missing/older-than-src as stale, and :74 runs the package's own `pnpm run build`, which package.json:21 defines as `build:shell && build:plugin` (:19-20 = `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` then `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`). The second alleged gap is also closed: build-if-stale.mjs:54 stats BOTH `vite.shell.config.ts` and `tsconfig.build.json` in `newestSourceMtime()`. The finding's cited evidence is simply not in the file: there is no `buildShellIfStale()` at verify-frame.mjs:82-91 (those lines are `shutdown()` and the start of `boot()`), no local `newestSourceMtime()` at line 106 (that line is inside boot()'s deadline loop), and a repo-wide grep for `buildShellIfStale` returns zero hits. verify-frame.mjs:113-121 and build-if-stale.mjs:6-18 explicitly document that this shell-only staleness trap is precisely why the helper was extracted and shared with verify-consumer.mjs (which uses it at :37/:174). Therefore a clean checkout builds dist/plugin/index.js before boot (no `Cannot find module`) and a dirty checkout rebuilds stale plugin bytes.
